sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Williamsport, PA different?
sections.html:
Williamsport is the seat of Lycoming County and the commercial center of north central Pennsylvania, so its housing market follows college calendars, hospital hiring and the river as much as it follows the wider region. Renters make up most households here, which affects who buys and what they expect from a property.

The Census Bureau estimates 27,384 residents for July 2025, down 1.3 percent from the 2020 base. Only 43.0 percent of housing units are owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024, the median home value is $154,300 and median gross rent is $855. The city counts 11,320 households with 2.14 people each, a median household income of $48,851 and a poverty rate of 25.4 percent.

Population peaked at 45,729 in 1930 when lumber money built the mansions on West Fourth Street. It stood at 27,754 in the 2020 census. That is a drop of about 40 percent from the 1930 peak.

sections.h2: What fees does the Williamsport Bureau of Codes charge?
sections.html:
The city's Bureau of Codes publishes a fee schedule, and several lines apply to owners who are selling or renting a property. It is open Monday to Friday from 8:00am to 4:00pm, closed for lunch from 12:00pm to 1:00pm, at 200 Reighard Ave., and the main number is (570) 327-7517.

Selected City of Williamsport Bureau of Codes fees from the city's published fee schedule
FeeAmount
Rental property inspection$85 per building plus $15 for each additional unit
Rental re-inspection$30 per visit
Zoning occupancy permit$60
Zoning, building, fire occupancy$100
Certification of zoning and building$50 per request
College letter inspection$60 per address plus $15 per unit

Most permits issue within 15 business days of a completed application, except new construction or major reconstruction. Ask the Bureau which occupancy or certification letter your buyer or lender expects, and request it early.

sections.h2: How does the Williamsport rental inspection affect a sale?
sections.html:
If the house has tenants or is used as student housing, the rental inspection fee schedule applies, and the Bureau lists inspection of rental properties among its core duties. A landlord selling a unit should find out whether the inspection is current and whether a re-inspection is open.

  • Gather any inspection reports and repair receipts for the buyer.
  • Check the unit count, because the fee grows with each unit in a building.
  • Sobriety houses, rooming houses and student residences have their own license line at $60 plus $15 per room, capped at $500.
  • Zoning matters for conversions. Variances and special exceptions each carry a $500 application fee, so confirm the legal use before you advertise a duplex or apartments.

A purchaser paying cash for a tenant-occupied building can accept the inspection history as is, yet the closing agent will still want clean paperwork on each unit.

sections.h2: Which Williamsport neighborhoods and schools shape buyer interest?
sections.html:
Williamsport's neighborhoods each draw a different buyer. Downtown runs between Hepburn Street and Basin Street, and Millionaires' Row along West Fourth Street is a National Register historic district. Newberry lies west of Lycoming Creek, Vallamont sits north of Rural Avenue, Grampian Hills spreads around Grampian Boulevard, Park Avenue and East End fill in the south and east, and West Hills occupies the hillside and hilltop.

The Williamsport Area School District serves the city with Cochran, Hepburn Lycoming and Jackson primary schools, Curtin and Lycoming Valley intermediate schools, a middle school and Williamsport Area High School. The district was recognized for its music program, and Stevens Primary School closed in 2022. Lycoming College and Pennsylvania College of Technology are both in the city, which keeps a steady pool of student renters and staff buyers.

Little League Baseball began here in 1939, and the Little League World Series is held every late summer in neighboring South Williamsport, a draw for visitors.

sections.h2: How do floods and winters affect a Williamsport house?
sections.html:
Water is the first thing buyers ask about. The West Branch Susquehanna River borders the city on the south, and the March 1936 flood crested at 33.9 feet and reached High Street. June 1972, when Hurricane Agnes struck, set the wettest month on record at 16.80 inches. A flood control levee and the Susquehanna Riverwalk now run along the river.

Winter is the second factor. Williamsport averages about 36 inches of snow a season, January is the coldest month, and the first freeze typically arrives around October 16, so roofs, gutters and heating systems get tested every year. Yearly precipitation averages roughly 43 inches over about 136 days, which keeps basement moisture on every inspector's list.

Gather your flood insurance history, any basement repair records and roof dates before you talk with a buyer. Those documents answer the questions that slow offers down.

sections.h2: How is a Williamsport deed recorded and taxed?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent realty transfer tax on the value transferred, and county recorders collect it along with any local tax. Both buyer and seller are jointly liable, and the contract decides who pays what. Some family transfers and transfers by will or intestate succession are exempt.

The Lycoming County Recorder of Deeds keeps land records back to 1795, with images online at the county's search portal. The county lists eleven school districts for transfer tax purposes, and Williamsport is one of them, so the local share can be divided between the municipality and the school district. Ask the Recorder or your title company for the exact local rate and the current recording fee before closing.

To add or remove a name, a new deed must be drawn and recorded. The county suggests a real estate attorney or title company for that job.

sections.h2: What should I prepare before listing a Williamsport house?
sections.html:
A short checklist saves weeks in a city with several overlapping offices: the Bureau of Codes on Reighard Avenue, the county Recorder downtown and the title company handling settlement.

  • Pull the parcel number and the names exactly as they appear on the deed.
  • Collect rental inspection letters, re-inspection results and any open permit paperwork.
  • Photograph the basement, roofline and any river-side flood marks, and keep insurance claims on hand.
  • Confirm the zoning use, particularly for duplexes, rooming houses and student residences.
  • Decide how you want to split the 1 percent state transfer tax and any local tax with the buyer.

With those items in a folder, you can compare a listing, a private sale and an as-is purchase on the same footing, and a buyer's questions get quick answers.

sections.h2: What do getting around and local jobs mean for Williamsport sellers?
sections.html:
Interstate 180, US 15 and US 220 meet at Williamsport, and Harrisburg is about 85 miles away. River Valley Transit runs local buses, Fullington Trailways connects downtown to Harrisburg, New York and Philadelphia, and Williamsport Regional Airport in Montoursville has flights to Washington Dulles. The Census puts the mean commute for 2020 to 2024 at 15.8 minutes.

Major employers include UPMC Susquehanna, Penn College, the school district and several manufacturers, including a large Lycoming Engines plant. The city sits in Marcellus Shale gas country, which has added another layer to the local economy. For sellers, that mix means buyers include nurses, instructors and plant workers who value short drives and move-in-ready homes.

faqs.q: Does the City of Williamsport require an inspection when I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the Bureau of Codes at (570) 327-7517, because the published fee schedule lists occupancy and certification letters that a lender or buyer may request. Rental properties have a separate inspection fee of $85 per building plus $15 per added unit.

faqs.q: How much is a rental inspection in Williamsport?
faqs.a: A rental property inspection costs $85 per building plus $15 for each additional unit in the building. A re-inspection visit costs $30.

faqs.q: Who records the deed on a Williamsport sale?
faqs.a: The Lycoming County Recorder of Deeds records it. Pennsylvania's 1 percent state realty transfer tax is collected there, together with any local tax and recording fee, and the deed is not recorded until payment is made.

faqs.q: Does flooding affect selling in Williamsport?
faqs.a: It can, because the city borders the West Branch Susquehanna River and has a flood history, including a 33.9 foot crest in 1936. Have your insurance and repair records ready, and any buyer will still ask about them.

faqs.q: How long does a permit take in Williamsport?
faqs.a: Most permits are issued within 15 business days of submitting the required application. New construction and major reconstruction can take longer.
